table: Table 2, Main Effects for Cognitions, Affect, Constraints, and Sample/Study Characteristics (dispositional rows)
title: The road to forgiveness: A meta-analytic synthesis of its situational and dispositional correlates
authors: Fehr, Gelfand and Nag (2010), Psychological Bulletin 136(5):894-914, doi 10.1037/a0019993
universe: Victims of a single offense by a single offender, in recall, scenario and survey studies (forgiveness of a spouse, friend, coworker or stranger)
geography: Studies from several countries; no place breakdown
limits: Correlations with forgiveness, not with holding a grudge after a job loss: the authors 'do not differentiate between measures of forgiveness (e.g., benevolence) and measures of unforgiveness (e.g., revenge)', so each r is read with its sign reversed as the pull toward keeping a grievance. A trait's pull on the choice, not a share of people; the game uses it only to check that personality turns some responses in the right direction and to a similar size (scripts/research/people-year.ts, src/core2/drives.test.ts).

dispositional.reading: Agreeable people forgive; low agreeableness keeps the grievance. The game's people-mind-v1:conflict trait is agreeableness compliance reversed (data/content/trait-act-pulls.json), so a high conflict level leans toward hold-grudge.

quote: For agreeableness, r = .22, indicating that agreeable people tend to forgive their offenders.
tableRow: Agreeableness: k = 10, total n = 1,732, mean r .21, weighted mean r .22, SE .02, 95% CI [.17, .27]. Neuroticism: k = 9, n = 1,551, weighted mean r -.24, 95% CI [-.32, -.16]. Trait anger: k = 18, n = 2,239, weighted mean r -.18, 95% CI [-.23, -.13].
use: The drives.respond row of data/research/trait-effect-sizes.json (option hold-grudge): the size of the pull a low-agreeableness temperament gives toward keeping a grievance, which the response model's trait-lean gain (responseTraitLeanGain) is checked against.
readVia: Full text read from the Psychological Bulletin PDF at https://ggsc.berkeley.edu/images/uploads/Fehr_et_al_2010_The_road_to_forgiveness-_A_meta-analytic_synthesis_of_its_situational_and_dispositional_correlates.pdf (text extracted with pdftotext).
